newsitem.title: UK: UK to outline new arms sales curbs Monday -- BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK to outline new arms sales curbs Monday -- BBC.

text.p: Britain, one of the world's leading arms exporters, will on Monday reveal plans to curb weapons sales to countries with poor human rights records, the BBC reported.
It said Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, who ordered a review of Britain's arms sales policy to make it more ethical, was likely to announce that Indonesia would be one of the affected states.

Although human rights groups accuse Indonesia of using British weapons for internal repression, Cook was nevertheless likely to give the go-ahead for the export of 16 British Aerospace Hawk fighters, the BBC said.
Government lawyers had concluded that it would be impossible to revoke export licences for the Hawks, which activists say have been used against opponents in the breakaway East Timor region.
A Foreign Office spokesman said Cook would outline the review in a written answer to parliament later on Monday. He declined to give further details.
The BBC said he would focus on restricting the supply of weapons such as riot control vehicles and light armoured personnel carriers which can be used for internal repression.
Earlier this month Cook, who wants to put human rights at the centre of Britain's foreign policy, unveiled a 12-point list of measures to clamp down on arms sales to undesirable countries.
He said Indonesia would be one of the affected countries but did not elaborate.
The government's challenge is to find a way of balancing the drive for greater human rights abroad with the interests of Britain's powerful arms industry, which employs a total of 400,000 people.
